question: Does the same ani- lexical family independently support li+ame morphology across Rarámuri varieties, beyond a single segmented Munérachi example?

evidence.source: Moreno Pineda & Valenzuela Romo, Coherencia discursiva en relatos ralámuli (tarahumara), Expedicionario 4 (2022)
evidence.assessment: Direct published segmentation of ani + -lí + -ame. This is the anchor analysis.

evidence.source: Manual Ralámuli Escrito para Todas y Todos, UPNECH et al. 2019, Tabla 2
evidence.assessment: Controlled intervariety table independently attests the surface form anilíame in the Western column; it does not itself provide morpheme segmentation.

forms: Uché bilé José napu Barsabasi anilime nile
evidence.assessment: Repeated natural-text use of anilime in naming/being-called contexts. The corpus confirms productivity and lexical identity in Western Rarámuri, but not an interlinear segmentation.

crossvariety_conclusion.constructional_inference: The simplest comparative reading is that Western anilíame/anilime belongs to the same ani- + li + ame construction directly segmented in Munérachi, but the Western segmentation remains an inference rather than an authored parse.

importance_for_project: This is the strongest same-root transvariety replication yet assembled for the li+ame bridge: one variety supplies direct morpheme-by-morpheme segmentation, while Western sources independently supply a controlled dialect-table form and repeated natural-text tokens in the same naming function.
epistemic_limits: Do not convert Western anilíame/anilime into a direct parse solely because Munérachi has ani-lí-ame.
Do not assume that -lí has exactly the same grammatical label in every variety; source labels differ (PSV/CE) and Western sources audited here are unsegmented.
Orthographic -ame/-ime variation is not itself treated as a sound law.
No historical cognacy judgment is performed in this artifact.
next_tests: Search for a Western grammar or interlinear corpus that explicitly segments anilíame/anilime.
Search for a third modern lexical root with a direct X-li-ame parse, keeping direct parses separate from paradigm-supported candidates.
Use ani- as the benchmark case when evaluating historical tsane-li-ameke versus modern li+ame constructional continuity.
